subject: Logging & Redaction follow-up — FinTechCo PII controls
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@fintechco.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: logging controls & redaction (FinTechCo)

Thanks again for the call today, Alex — appreciate you and the security team's time. Quick recap and next steps so we keep things moving on your security review: 

Summary of what we covered:
- High-level ask: how request/response logging is handled for Redwood inference (payloads, headers, trace IDs) and options for masking/redaction and retention.
- Context: FinTechCo requires no unredacted PII stored in logs for production workloads; retention window requested is <= 30 days for debug logs, with ability to export to customer-managed storage for audit.

Our proposed options (high level):
1) Hosted API (Redwood-managed):
   - Default: capture metadata (timestamps, model, route, token counts) + deterministic hashes of payloads for dedup/troubleshooting.
   - Payloads: can be configured to be fully redacted (no plaintext stored) or masked using configurable rules (regex-based).
   - Headers/trace IDs: we can redact or hash specific headers (e.g., Authorization, X-Trace-ID). Trace IDs can be retained in hashed form to correlate requests without exposing raw IDs.
   - Retention: default 90 days but configurable per-customer; we can set a 30-day policy for FinTechCo during onboarding.
2) Dedicated or Private deployment:
   - Option to disable forwarding of request/response payloads to Redwood control plane entirely.
   - Logs can be routed to customer-managed S3/VPC collector or on-prem HSM/ELK for full control and retention rules.

Attachments I sent for your review: redwood-logging-controls.pdf (detailed options) and SOC2-section-logs.pdf (audit excerpt).

Next steps I propose:
- I'll share a short redaction policy template and a sample regex list for common PII patterns (credit card, SSN, email).
- Rishi (SE) will join a technical deep-dive next week to walk through architecture and run a demo of the redaction rules in our staging environment.
- If acceptable, we'll capture the short mutual action plan and target a small pilot (non-production) to validate behavior.

Are you available for a technical deep-dive Wednesday or Thursday next week?

Thanks,

--

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: logging controls & redaction (FinTechCo)

Thanks Marissa — very helpful summary. A few clarifying Qs from our security desk so we can include accurate answers in the internal review: 

1) When you say "request/response payloads can be fully redacted," does that mean raw prompt + model output are never stored in any Redwood-managed logs for that customer? Or are they stored encrypted/hashed for a bounded retention window?

2) For headers and trace IDs: we need to ensure that X-Trace-ID and any correlation IDs that may contain customer-provided identifiers are not logged in plaintext. Can you confirm whether trace IDs are present in any hosted debugging traces, and what controls we have to remove/hash them?

3) For Hosted API: can logs be pushed to our S3 bucket (cross-account) or to a collector in our VPC instead of stored in Redwood's control plane? If not, what assurances do we have around encryption-at-rest and key management?

4) Are redaction rules applied at the ingestion boundary (before logs hit persistent storage), or do they run as post-processing jobs? From a compliance standpoint we prefer ingestion-time redaction.

5) Any sample regex/policy docs you can share would be great — and if possible an example showing a credit-card number masked vs removed entirely.

If we can get concrete answers to these, we should be able to move forward to the pilot. Wednesday afternoon (PST) works for me for the technical deep-dive.

Alex
Head of Security — FinTechCo
alex.j@fintechco.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@fintechco.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: logging controls & redaction (FinTechCo)

Great questions, Alex — answers below (high level). I've looped Rishi (SE) and Vivek (Head of Platform Security) to add any technical detail and confirm operational runbooks.

1) Storage of payloads (hosted):
   - We support two modes for hosted customers:
     a) No-payload mode: payloads (prompts + responses) are not persisted in Redwood-managed logs at all. We keep only deterministic hashes and metadata for deduplication and troubleshooting.
     b) Masked/redacted mode: ingestion-time redaction applies configurable rules (see #4) to remove or mask PII before persistence. Encrypted-at-rest always; customers may also request SSE-KMS where we use a customer-managed CMK for hosted logs.

2) Trace IDs and headers:
   - By default, trace IDs (X-Trace-ID) are captured in internal traces for correlation but can be configured to be hashed or removed for a given customer or route.
   - Specific headers (Authorization, Cookie, X-User-Email, etc.) can be blacklisted and removed at the ingestion gateway. We store a small set of sanitized header metadata for routing/debugging.

3) Log routing to customer storage:
   - Hosted: we can export structured logs to a customer S3 bucket (cross-account) or to a customer-managed collector in your VPC via Kinesis/Firehose. This is a common pattern for customers with strict retention controls.
   - Dedicated/Private: logs can be kept entirely in your environment (no copy to Redwood control plane) if you opt for Private deployment.

4) Redaction timing and guarantees:
   - Redaction is applied at ingestion (gateway) in all our supported configurations for PII policies — we do not rely on post-processing for deletions in compliance-sensitive setups.
   - Redaction rules are regex-based with optional named capture groups; we also support token-preserving masks (e.g., replace middle digits with asterisks) and full removal.

5) Samples and policy templates: attached is a short redaction-policy template (redwood-redaction-policy-templates.docx) with example regex snippets for credit card, SSN, and common account IDs. Example: credit card mask rule -> replace with 16-digit-preserving mask: "**** **** **** 1234".

Operational notes:
- Debugging & support: when support-level access is needed for live debugging we require a signed access request. For hosted customers that have chosen no-payload mode, support can request session-level ephemeral replay with customer approval; ephemeral logs are short-lived (max 48 hours) and auditable.
- Retention: we can set a 30-day retention policy for FinTechCo logs in hosted mode; for longer audit retention you can push exports to your S3.

Next steps:
- Confirm Wednesday 14:00 PST for the technical deep-dive (Rishi will demo ingestion-time redaction and the S3 export flow).
- I'll also circulate the mutual action plan doc and proposed pilot scope after the call.

Thanks,

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: logging controls & redaction (FinTechCo) — SE notes

Adding a few technical specifics to Marissa's answers so you have concrete detail for the security review: 

- Masking vs redaction: masking replaces matched tokens with a deterministic or length-preserving mask (e.g., 4111-****-****-1111) while redaction removes the token entirely. Both are applied before persistence at the ingestion gateway.
- Regex examples (from the template):
   - Credit card (Visa/Mastercard): (?:(?:4\d{3})|(?:5[1-5]\d{2}))[- ]?\d{4}[- ]?\d{4}[- ]?\d{4}
   - SSN (US): (?!000|666)(\d{3})[- ]?(?!00)(\d{2})[- ]?(?!0000)(\d{4})
- Trace IDs: we can hash X-Trace-ID with HMAC-SHA256 using a per-customer key so the value is stable for correlation but irreversible for anyone without the key.
- Ingestion pipeline: redaction hooks sit in the edge gateway (Envoy filter) so they run before logs are emitted to storage.
- Embeddings & indexing: we recommend not sending raw PII to embedding routes. If you must, we support a scrubbed-embedding route that applies the same redaction rules before vectorization.

I'll demo these during the deep-dive and can show the live masking rules in the staging UI.

-Rishi
